newsitem.title: USA: PSA expects U.S. GDP growth at 2.2 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: PSA expects U.S. GDP growth at 2.2 pct in 1997.

text.p: U.S. Gross Domestic Product is expected to grow by an average of 2.2 percent in 1997 on a fourth-quarter to fourth-quarter basis against 2.6 percent increase seen for 1996, PSA The Bond Market Association said.
"This is an excellent and continued performance of the economy," Frederick Breimyer, co-chairman of the PSA's Economic Advisory Committee, told reporters here.

The PSA Committee, which represents a consensus forecast of 11 economists from major Wall Street and regional securities firms and banks, also said it expects Republicans and Democrats to reach a balanced-budget agreement in 1997.
The PSA Committee forecast U.S. consumer price index (CPI) will rise by 3.0 percent in 1997 against an estimated 3.1 percent rise in 1996.

The average unemployment rate is expected to stay at 5.3 percent in 1997 versus an average forecast of 5.4 percent in 1996. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond yield is expected to be at 6.8 percent by December 1997 against an expected 6.5 percent in December 1996.
The Committee sees short-term rates stable in 1997, with the federal funds trading between 5.25 and 5.50 percent.
